name: CREST
fullName: Stenting versus Endarterectomy for Carotid-Artery Stenosis
teachingPoint: No significant difference between CAS and CEA on the composite; periprocedural stroke favored CEA and periprocedural MI favored CAS, and 4-year stroke or death (secondary endpoint) was higher with CAS (6.4% vs 4.7%; HR 1.50, p=0.03).

name: CREST-2
fullName: Medical Management and Revascularization for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis
population: n=2485, adults, NIHSS ASYMPTOMATIC high-grade (>=70%) carotid stenosis, follow-up to 4 years
finding: Stenting trial POSITIVE: 2.8% vs 6.0% medical alone. Endarterectomy trial NEUTRAL: 3.7% vs 5.3%
teachingPoint: In asymptomatic >=70% stenosis on intensive medical therapy, adding stenting reduced 4-year events; adding endarterectomy did not reach significance.

name: ECST-2
fullName: Optimised Medical Therapy Alone versus Optimised Medical Therapy plus Revascularisation for Carotid Stenosis — 2-year interim results
population: n=429, >=18, NIHSS asymptomatic or symptomatic carotid stenosis >=50% with LOW-to-INTERMEDIATE predicted risk (5-year ipsilateral stroke risk <20% by Carotid Artery Risk score), 2-year interim analysis
finding: No benefit from added revascularization in this low-to-intermediate-risk group
teachingPoint: For carotid stenosis with a low-to-intermediate predicted stroke risk, adding revascularization to optimised medical therapy showed no 2-year benefit.
